newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey-Israel military exercises to go ahead.
newsitem.headline: Turkey-Israel military exercises to go ahead.

text.p: Turkish officials said on Wednesday that Ankara was going ahead with plans to hold joint naval exercises with Israel, despite comments by Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan suggesting they may be postponed.
"There is no question of such a postponement...At the moment it is not clear when these exercises will take place," Defence Minister Turhan Tayan told a news conference.
He said work was in progress to clarify details of the exercises and set a date.
"Such work is done by the general staff and there is no question of the prime minister approving or postponing of his own accord," Tayan said.
Turkey's Foreign Ministry spokesman had earlier also denied any postponement.

Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, suggested earlier that the exercises, part of a military accord between the two countries, might be postponed, according to the state-run Anatolian news agency.
But he gave no details and it was not clear what kind of postponement he was referring to.
NATO member Turkey has signed two military accords with Israel allowing Israeli military jets to use Turkish airspace for training flights and to upgrade its own ageing F-4 fighters in Israel.
Turkey's military reached agreement on joint naval exercises with Israel and the United States last week, both undermining Erbakan and serving notice on regional rivals Syria, Iran and Iraq.

"We are talking to our brothers in Turkey about this issue. Turkey is welcome to hold exercises but they must not be directed against anyone or aimed at putting pressure on any Arab country," President Hosni Mubarak of Egypt said late on Tuesday.
The Turkish Foreign Ministry has said the naval exercises, set to take place some time in mid-year, do not threaten neighbouring countries.
It said the manoeuvres would not have any strategic purpose and would be focused on search and rescue operations.
Erbakan promised to scrap the military accords with Israel before coming to power last June and replace them with closer ties with the Arab and Moslem world.
However bilateral ties with the Jewish state have flourished under the army's patronage throughout Erbakan's term of office, unnerving his grassroots supporters.
